# Multo (song)
"Multo" (lit. "Ghost") is a song by the Filipino alternative pop band Cup of Joe. It was released on September 14, 2024, by Viva Records as the lead single from the band’s debut album Silakbo (2025). The song was co-written by Cup of Joe’s vocalist Raphaell “Rapha” Ridao together with his older brother Immanuel Ridao during the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020. Produced by Shadiel Chan (with co-production by Jovel Rivera), "Multo" is an emotional synth-driven pop-rock ballad about the lingering “ghost” of a past love and the pain of unresolved grief.
Upon its release, "Multo" gradually became a viral hit and a breakthrough for Cup of Joe, garnering widespread popularity on streaming and social media platforms. In the Philippines, it topped the national music charts for a record-setting run of 27 consecutive weeks in 2025. The track also gained international traction: it entered the Billboard Global 200 chart in April 2025 – marking the first ever entry by a Filipino act – and eventually peaked at No. 80 on that global chart. The song reached as high as No. 28 on Spotify’s daily Global Top 50, the highest position for any Filipino song to date. By May 2025, "Multo" had accumulated over 60 million streams on Spotify, and it continued to trend internationally through countless TikTok and Instagram videos featuring its theme of love and heartbreak.
Background and release: Cup of Joe is a five-member pop-rock band from Baguio, Philippines. In mid-2020, during pandemic quarantine, lead singer Raphaell Ridao and his brother began writing "Multo" as a way to channel their feelings of loneliness and loss. According to Ridao, they poured all their longing and sadness into the song, finding “a sense of relief” after doing so. The song’s lyrics, in the Filipino language, describe how one is “haunted” by memories of a lost love – no matter where one goes or how much time passes – until those emotions are finally confronted. The title "Multo", which means ghost, symbolizes the persistent emotional shadow left by a past relationship. Musically, the track marked a stylistic shift for Cup of Joe; it is a melancholic synth-pop ballad with pop-rock elements, contrasting with the upbeat pop sound of some of their earlier works. The band members have noted that "Multo" was more experimental and ambitious in sound, featuring a poignant chorus and atmospheric hook that immediately resonated with listeners.
Cup of Joe announced "Multo" unexpectedly, giving fans only a few hours’ notice on the day of release. The single was surprise-revealed on the afternoon of September 13, 2024, and officially released later that night. It was issued as the first single from Silakbo, the band’s debut studio album which would arrive in January 2025. Silakbo is a concept album themed around the five stages of grief, and "Multo" appears as the seventh track, representing the “depression” stage of the album’s narrative arc. Upon release, the song initially received modest attention, but its heartfelt theme and relatable lyrics quickly struck a chord with listeners. By late 2024, Cup of Joe’s prior singles like “Misteryoso” and “Tingin” had charted locally, and "Multo" built on this momentum. The song’s popularity snowballed in early 2025 through word of mouth and social media – especially TikTok, where users set personal videos and breakup stories to the "Multo" soundtrack, making the song a viral audio for themes of heartbreak and “ghosting”. This organic online exposure helped propel "Multo" to the top of streaming charts in the Philippines and eventually onto international charts.
Music and lyrics: "Multo" is characterized by its lush synthesizer-driven sound and emotive pop-rock instrumentation. The production (handled by Shadiel Chan, with Jovel Rivera) blends gentle keyboards and ambient guitar work with a slow-building rhythm, creating a haunting, melancholic atmosphere. The band’s co-lead vocalists, Raphaell Ridao and Gian Bernardino, deliver an impassioned performance, conveying the song’s themes of regret and lingering heartache. Lyrically, "Multo" is written entirely in Filipino, filled with poetic imagery of darkness and haunting to depict the aftermath of a painful breakup. Critics and the band members have noted that the song’s central metaphor – being followed by a “ghost” of one’s feelings – encapsulates the difficulty of moving on from lost love. In one notable line, “Hindi na ba mamamayapa?” (translated as “Am I never going to be at peace?”), the narrator expresses frustration at the thought that they may never find emotional closure. The chorus — “Pasindi na ng ilaw / Minumulto na ’ko ng damdamin ko” (“Turn on the lights / I am being haunted by my emotions”) — vividly conveys the feeling of being trapped in a darkness by unresolved feelings. These candid, heartfelt lyrics resonated strongly with listeners who had undergone similar experiences. Billboard Philippines described "Multo" as an “emotional, synth-driven track” that delivers a poignant exploration of “the ghosts of our past” and how one is “constantly haunted by the memory of lost love”. The song’s style and subject matter marked a new musical chapter for Cup of Joe, showcasing more mature songwriting. Rolling Stone later called "Multo" an “artistic awakening” for the band and evidence of their growth as “serious pop storytellers,” highlighting the song’s ability to linger in the listener’s mind after one full listen.
Music video: The official music video for "Multo" was released on March 6, 2025, about six months after the single. Directed by Kris Ulrich Cazin, the video features Filipino actors Miles Ocampo and Elijah Canlas portraying a couple torn apart by heartbreak. In the cinematic narrative, Ocampo’s character is shown grappling with bittersweet memories of a past romance — the “ghosts” of her former love — which manifest in scenes throughout their old home. Canlas appears as the lost lover in flashbacks and as a phantom-like presence in the empty rooms, symbolizing how the memories continue to haunt her. The video’s somber, artful visuals (lit with chiaroscuro lighting to evoke an eerie, nostalgic mood) reinforce the song’s themes of love and loss. As the song builds to its chorus, Ocampo’s character is seen turning on lights in a dark house, directly mirroring the lyric “Pasindi na ng ilaw” (“light up the lights”) as she seeks relief from the multo of her emotions. Cup of Joe themselves make cameo appearances performing the song with subdued passion, intercut with the storyline. The music video’s release was highly anticipated by fans — the band had teased the project in late February 2025 and even held a special launch event for it in Quezon City, which sold out within an hour. Upon release, the video was praised for its storytelling and the performances of Ocampo and Canlas, who are both noted young actors. Critics remarked that the visual treatment added depth to the song, effectively translating the “hauntingly beautiful” quality of "Multo" into a short film about love, grief, and acceptance. The music video quickly garnered millions of views on YouTube, further fueling the song’s popularity. (By September 2025, the various uploads of "Multo" – including official and lyric videos – had accumulated nearly 20 million combined views on YouTube.)
Commercial performance: "Multo" became one of the most successful OPM (Original Pilipino Music) songs of the mid-2020s. In the Philippines, it achieved massive chart dominance. The single reached No. 1 on the inaugural Billboard Philippines Hot 100 in April 2025 and remained at the top spot for 27 consecutive weeks. This streak set a record for the longest-running number-one song since the chart’s establishment, solidifying "Multo" as a fixture on Filipino airwaves and streaming playlists throughout 2025. Even as numerous other hits emerged, "Multo" maintained its lead, outperforming both local releases and popular international tracks in the country over several months. The song also topped Billboard’s Top Philippine Songs weekly chart for the same duration, underscoring its cross-platform popularity. By year’s end, "Multo" was officially the most-streamed song of 2025 in the Philippines on Spotify. The band Cup of Joe was likewise named Spotify’s top local artist of the year, largely propelled by the song’s performance.
Internationally, "Multo" marked a breakthrough for Filipino music on the global stage. Thanks to strong streaming numbers and virality, the track entered the Billboard Global 200 chart (which ranks the world’s most popular songs) in the issue dated April 22, 2025. It debuted at No. 181 on that chart, making Cup of Joe the first Filipino act in history to appear on the Global 200. In the same week, "Multo" also charted on the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. listing at No. 74 – the first time a Filipino song had reached the top 100 of that ranking. Following its debut, "Multo" continued to rise in global popularity; it eventually peaked at number 80 on the Billboard Global 200 in the subsequent weeks. This achievement was hailed as a significant milestone for OPM, as no Filipino-language song had ever climbed so high on an international chart before. On Spotify’s worldwide charts, "Multo" performed impressively as well. In mid-2025, it climbed into the Top 30 of Spotify’s Global daily songs chart, reaching around the #28 position at peak. The song also amassed a large international listenership on platforms like YouTube and Apple Music, aided by its inclusion in various global playlists and algorithmic recommendations. By late 2025, Cup of Joe reported having over 10 million monthly listeners on Spotify – the highest for any Filipino artist at the time – attributable in large part to the runaway success of "Multo".
Accolades and impact: "Multo" earned Cup of Joe critical acclaim and several honors. In October 2025, the song won “Song of the Year” at the inaugural Filipino Music Awards, held at the Mall of Asia Arena. This award recognized "Multo" for its impact and popularity, and the band also took home “Album of the Year” for Silakbo during the same event. Earlier in 2025, "Multo" had been nominated in various local award programs and was consistently lauded by media for revitalizing OPM’s presence on the global scene. The song’s commercial and streaming feats led to Billboard Philippines honoring Cup of Joe with a special recognition plaque in October 2025, commemorating "Multo"’s record-breaking 27-week reign at No. 1 on the charts. Beyond awards, "Multo" became a cultural phenomenon in the Philippines. It inspired countless covers, renditions, and social media trends – from acoustic covers by other OPM artists to dance challenge videos (despite being a ballad) interpreting the song’s emotional story. The track was also used in popular Filipino TV shows, web series, and short films as an anthem for heartbreak. Notably, fans of a prominent teen drama pairing (actor Will Ashley and actress Bianca de Vera) adopted "Multo" as an unofficial “theme song” for the couple, further spreading the song’s exposure online.
Industry observers credit "Multo" with helping usher in a new wave of global interest in Filipino music. The band has expressed gratitude that their very Filipino-specific song — sung entirely in Tagalog and rooted in local sentiment — resonated with a worldwide audience. Cup of Joe’s members noted that the song’s success proved that OPM could “make waves internationally” and opened doors for more Filipino acts to be recognized abroad. By the end of 2025, "Multo" had firmly secured its place as one of the most iconic OPM songs of the decade, with many Filipino listeners considering it an anthem of heartbreak and healing. Its enduring popularity was reflected in Spotify’s 2025 Wrapped report, where "Multo" ranked as the #1 Local Song of the Year in the Philippines. The song’s emotional message, combined with its record-breaking achievements, have positioned "Multo" as a modern classic in Philippine pop music, often being referred to in media as a “ghostly hit” that transcended its humble beginnings to haunt charts and hearts worldwide.

Cup of Joe's 'Multo' has made it to the Billboard Global 200!

OPM pride is on full display as Filipino band [Cup of Joe](https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/showbiznews/news/119334/cup-of-joe-ready-to-perform-new-songs-for-their-joewahs-in-2-night-silakbo-concert/story) finally makes waves on the international charts.

Making OPM history, Cup of Joe's chart-topping track "[Multo](https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/showbiznews/news/121604/cup-of-joes-rapha-shares-the-story-behind-viral-song-multo/story)" has landed at no.181 on the Billboard Global 200.

The Filipino band's hit song ranks ahead of international releases like “Handlebars” by Jennie and Dua Lipa (no. 186) and Rosé's “Toxic Til The End” (no. 194), showing just how far OPM can go.

Composed of vocalists Gian Bernardino and Rapha Ridao, lead guitarist Gab Fernandez, rhythm guitarist CJ Fernandez, and keyboardist Xen Gareza, the OPM band got netizens, especially TikTok users, singing along and using "Multo" in their random and relapse videos.

According to Rapha, he wrote “Multo” with his brother Immanuel Ridao in 2020.

Rapha explained on his Instagram, “Nilabas namin doon lahat ng mga feelings namin na longing \[at\] lahat ng lungkot na hindi namin inakalang kaya namin harapin. After namin nasulat 'yung song, parang mayroon 'yung sense of relief. Para bang nawalan ng bigat 'yung dibdib namin."

“It's about na kahit saan ka pumunta, sinusundan ka pa rin ng mga nararamdaman mo kasi it's part of being human na kahit anong gawin mo, nandiyan pa rin. Kahit ilang taon nang nakalipas, bigla mo na lang maaalala na 'di ka lilisanin. Minumulto ka nga ng damdamin mo,” he added.

"Multo" was released in 2024 and was also featured on the band's debut album, _Silakbo_, which dropped in January.

On March 6, the OPM band released the official music video starring [Elijah Canlas](https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/celebritylife/hobbies/121044/elijah-canlas-turns-badminton-into-a-platform-for-mental-health-awareness/story) and Miles Ocampo.

Cup of Joe is also known for their songs "Misteryoso," "Tingin," "Estranghero," and "Ikaw Pa Rin Ang Piliin Ko."

“Haunted by My Emotions”: The Story Behind Cup of Joe's “Multo”
===============================================================

[![Image 6: Dinar Maharani Hasnadi](https://seasia.co/img/users/users_YBy9zS8EdL.png?p=users-sm)](https://seasia.co/u/dinarmaharani)By [Dinar Maharani Hasnadi](https://seasia.co/u/dinarmaharani)

July 28, 2025 12:53 PM GMT+7 4 mins

![Image 7: “Haunted by My Emotions”: The Story Behind Cup of Joe's “Multo”](https://seasia.co/front/img/placeholder-857x400.jpg?v=202315-0723-0054)

Cup of Joe's "Multo" has become an international hit (Source: Billboard Philippines)

What do you do after a breakup? You may take a walk, find a new hobby, or download a dating app to look for a new partner. Yet, most of the time, breakups, and loss in general, can be so painful that it may take quite a while for us before doing those things and moving on.

Baguio-based Filipino pop-rock band, Cup of Joe, has successfully portrayed that post-breakup emotional haunting in their hit song, “Multo”. Marking their attempt at a new genre of music, the tune not only brought Cup of Joe to the international music stage, but also touched the hearts of many people experiencing the same pain.

A Tale of Love and Loss
-----------------------

![Image 8](https://cdn2.gnfi.net/seasia/uploads/images/11549/ab67616d0000b273394048503e3be0e65e962638jpeg)

The album cover for "Multo" (Source: Spotify | Cup of Joe)

It is said that heartbreak gives birth to the best artists. “Multo” was written by Raphaell “Rapha” Ridao, Cup of Joe's lead vocalist and songwriter, along with his brother Redentor during the Covid-19 pandemic. The loneliness they felt during quarantine led them to transform their feelings into song lyrics.

Produced by Shadiel Chan, an experienced music producer and CEO of a record label called Nine Degrees North, the song was released under Viva Records. In his personal Instagram post, Raphaell leaked an initial acoustic demo of the song, thanking his closest people for the support they showered him during his music career.

“Multo” features themes of loneliness, grief, and the emotional difficulty of dealing with loss. The song encapsulates that specific feeling when you feel like you've already moved on, but the image of the thing or person you lost still appears in your mind like a ghost. There's this frustration in your head when you just can't seem to shake those old memories off, and you don't understand what's going on or why you feel that way.

The catchy lyrics “_Hindi na ba ma-mamamayapa?_”, which translates to “am I never going to be at peace?” portrays the exact anger someone feels when things just don't seem to get any better, even after a considerable amount of time has passed since the breakup or painful event.

Yet, it is perhaps the chorus that has captured the hearts of countless music enjoyers: “_Pasindi na ng ilaw/Minumulto na ko ng damdamin ko_”, which translates to “Turn on the lights/I'm being haunted by my emotions”. This verse signifies the despair someone feels when they so badly want to get out of loneliness, which may feel like darkness at times.

Cup of Joe's New Start
----------------------

![Image 9](https://cdn2.gnfi.net/seasia/uploads/images/11549/bbph-web-discover-cup-of-joe-1600x838jpg)

Cup of Joe (Source: Billboard Philippines)

“Multo” is a groundbreaking moment for Cup of Joe, which used to produce boyband-style, upbeat pop music with choreographed dances and fan interactions onstage. As the seventh track in their debut album, _Silakbo_ (“Outburst”) – released in January 2025 – “Multo” is a melancholic, pop-rock ballad about heartbreak, something Cup of Joe had never really tried before.

_Rolling Stone_, the renowned pop culture magazine, calls “Multo” an “artistic awakening” and a mark of Cup of Joe's arrival as “serious pop storytellers”. Gabriel Saulog, host and lead writer at Billboard Philippines, states that though the attempt in switching musical genres may come off as a “surprise… ambitious and experimental”, “Multo” also “lingers deep upon its first full listen”.

This means that “Multo” isn't just a gift for Cup of Joe's fans – dubbed “JOEwahs” – going through loss, but also a sign that the band itself is experiencing some kind of renewal.

This may be especially true, considering the band itself experienced loss after bassist Raphael “Sevi” Severino decided to part ways just three months before “Multo” was released as a single in September 2024.

International Success
---------------------

![Image 10](https://cdn2.gnfi.net/seasia/uploads/images/11549/screenshot-20250722-192342-youtubejpg)

Cup of Joe performing "Multo" live at The Cozy Cove (Source: YouTube | Nine Degrees North)

“Multo” hit global ranks precisely because many people had similar experiences. TikTok users have shared their personal stories, relating the song's lyrics to memories of exes and lost lovers – those people you didn't even date, but somehow stick in your mind forever. In addition, the song's lyrics are written entirely in Filipino, boasting local richness and authenticity.

Garnering over 1,7 million plays as of May 2025, [“Multo” is the most-played song in Spotify Philippines, showcasing the love Filipinos have for a local artist lineup.](https://seasia.co/infographic/top-5-songs-on-spotify-in-southeast-asian-countries) In the international music industry, the song even ranked number 80 at Billboard Global 200, making Cup of Joe the first Filipino artist to enter the chart.

When this article was written, the music video of “Multo” has garnered more than 13 million views on YouTube, its lyric video more than 67 million views, and a live version of the performance at a restaurant called The Cozy Cove more than 43 million views. Instagram users have also demanded Cup of Joe to release an acoustic version, as posted in Raphaell Ridao's leak.

**Published** May 1, 2025 10:20am

Locked in the four walls of their house during the lockdown restrictions, Cup of Joe lead vocalist Rapha Ridao and his brother, Red, poured out their emotions and gave birth to the hit song "Multo."

Little did they know that the song will come crashing into the [Billboard Global 200 charts](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942862/cup-of-joe-multo-billboard-global-200/story/) five years later and help catapult the band into a different level of success.

"Kaming dalawa (ng kuya ko) 'yung nagsulat nung pandemic kasi nung time na 'yung 'di kami makalabas, wala kaming ibang (alam) gawin. It gave us time to reflect din kasi there's no escape nung (time) na 'yun eh," Ridao told GMA News in an interview.

Released in 2024, "Multo" has since fetched more than 60 million streams on Spotify. It's become so popular on TikTok, and has been used as an unofficial love song for popular [PBB love team](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942027/cup-of-joe-gian-bernardino-will-ashley-bianca-de-vera/story/) Will Ashley and Bianca de Vera.

With listeners having different interpretations and entries to the viral hit, Cup of Joe discussed the meaning behind the song and how important it is to them to raise the flag of OPM after the song's success.

**Shadows of the Past**

In 2020, Rapha was feeling a lot of things with the pandemic and felt like something was holding him back.

"Naumpisahan namin 'yung song with the thought of some feeling, some people feel things na kahit ano'ng gawin mo, kahit pilit mong nilalayo, sumusunod sa'yo," he recalled.

With the idea of someone following a person, the singer thought of a ghost or "multo" in Filipino and worked on the song with the said word.

"Napunta sa 'min 'yung thought na what if we use 'yung 'multo' as a figure na sinusundan ka. 'Yung feeling na 'yun, 'yung medyo scary," he said.

For Rapha, he wanted the listeners to feel how it's like to be haunted by your unexplainable thoughts and the past like a ghost.

"Gusto naming mapadama sa kanila 'yung element of being haunted. 'Yung feeling na parang wala ka namang nakikita pero andun pa rin eh, andun 'yung bigat. 'Yung mga emotions that can't be explained naturally 'yung mga ganoon," he said.

With the idea of making their album, "Multo" also helped Cup of Joe to circle around the five stages of grief with their album "Silakbo" released in January.

While the song quickly gained traction, processing its success was slow and enduring.

“Actually na-feel lang namin nung time na nagpahinga kami, nag-break from gigs tas doon namin nakikita na ‘ito na pala ‘yun’ ‘yung song na ‘to, No. 1 na,” said Gab Fernandez.

“Hindi namin siya ma-feel nang maayos kasi hindi kami magkakasama pero parang nung nagkasama-sama na kami parang doon lang namin na-feel ‘yung success namin,” he added.

Lead vocalist Gian Bernardino was glad with the reception of the song stressing how the varying interpretations of people with the song are valid.

"It goes along with the other songs na ni-release namin. We created the song with an initial thought then we shared it with the world then they came off with a different perspective and interpretation of the song," the singer said.

"Dahil doon marami rin kaming natututunang perspective which inspires us, which motivates us. Kung ano man 'yung interpretation niyo ng 'Multo,' it's all valid," he added.

**Long Overdue**

Recently reaching 10 million monthly listeners on Spotify — the most for a Filipino act — Cup of Joe stands among the likes of equally successful OPM acts like Juan Karlos, BINI, and Earl Agustin. Gian is just proud to be in the elite cadre.

“Nakaka-proud, we're very thankful na part kami ng generation ng OPM na talagang nare-recognize internationally,” he said.

Keyboardist Xen Gareza is quick to point to social media in helping them reach a wider audience, saying "'yung generation natin, we have the platform to reach international audiences so that's a big help and I believe na even then 'yung talent ng OPM talagang meron na."

“It's only now that we have the platform to go global or to reach further audiences na nare-recognize na rin nila 'yung skills ng Filipinos making art, music,” he added.

Gian stressed how it’s “long overdue” for more OPM acts to gain recognition internationally and it’s time for more artists to join them.

“Actually, long overdue na eh. OPM is very beautiful. It's very unique. It's something na could make waves internationally and I think it's time na rin kasi dati pa talaga dapat 'to. We're glad na we're part of that movement or mechanism na nag-start ng pagkilala ng mundo sa OPM,” he said.

Rafa and CJ Fernandez thanked their supporters and stressed how they made their success possible.

“Thank you kasi ever since 'yung support niyo ramdam na ramdam namin dito (sa puso) ... We're gonna make you guys happy and show you the love na pinapakita niyo sa amin,” Rafa said.

“Sobrang excited namin sa mga following months pa para sa lahat ng mangyayari kaya ayun sana abangan niyo,” CJ added.

Right now, Gian said that they are in the works of introducing more of the other songs in the “Silakbo” album to their listeners noting how there’s more to show with the tracks.

“Gusto lang namin sabihin, you're gonna like this, you've been waiting for this pero in terms of our music, we still have the whole year to introduce the whole album to, not only the Philippines but to the whole world, kasi there's more to see, to hear, to know about the 'Silakbo' album,” he said.

That, and relishing the moment's success.

"As a band we're very much immersing ourselves at the moment, kumbaga, we're living the moment. We're not really pressuring ourselves to achieve greater heights at where we are right now,” the lead vocalist said.

“As much as possible, we do our best every time and bonus na lang kung ano 'yung magiging reception ng tao,” he added. **— LA, GMA Integrated News**

Cup of Joe marks one year of hit song 'Multo': 'Thank you for making it a part of your journey'
===============================================================================================

By GMA Integrated News

**Published** September 16, 2025 11:08am  

![Image 9: Cup of Joe marks one year of hit song 'Multo': 'Thank you for making it a part of your journey'](https://images.gmanews.tv/webpics/2025/04/multo_2025_04_15_18_50_23.jpg)

Photo: Cup of Joe/IG

It’s been a year since Cup of Joe dropped their megahit, “Multo.”

The OPM pop rock band marked the “Multo-versary” occasion with an Instagram post.

“One year ago, we released ‘Multo’ and it found a home in your stories, heartbreaks, and healing,” Cup of Joe said.

“Thank you for making it a part of your journey,” the band added.

Other Stories
-------------

[### Cup of Joe drops new single ‘Sandali’](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/958629/cup-of-joe-drops-new-single-sandali/story/ "Cup of Joe drops new single ‘Sandali’")

[### Cup of Joe announces dates and venues for US-Canada tour](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/956555/cup-of-joe-announces-dates-and-venues-for-us-canada-tour/story/ "Cup of Joe announces dates and venues for US-Canada tour")

[### Cup of Joe adds third day to 'Stardust' concert in October](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/954433/cup-of-joe-adds-third-day-to-stardust-concert-in-october/story/ "Cup of Joe adds third day to 'Stardust' concert in October")

Cup of Joe’s "Multo" was included in their debut album "[Silakbo](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/hobbiesandactivities/933185/cup-of-joe-drops-debut-album-silakbo/story/)."

A song about the shadows of the past, “[Multo](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/944589/the-making-of-multo-and-the-rise-of-opm-band-cup-of-joe-to-global-success/story/)” became the soundtrack to [TikToks and Instagram posts](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news//lifestyle/content/942027/cup-of-joe-gian-bernardino-will-ashley-bianca-de-vera/story/) about topics like love, alternate universes, and heartbreaks.

In April, the song made it to the [Billboard Global 200](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/content/942862/cup-of-joe-multo-billboard-global-200/story/).

Cup of Joe is set to have three sold-out [Stardust concerts](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/954433/cup-of-joe-adds-third-day-to-stardust-concert-in-october/story/) at the Araneta Coliseum on October 10, 11, and 12.

Their latest song, “[Sandali](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/showbiz/chikaminute/958629/cup-of-joe-drops-new-single-sandali/story/),” came out this month.

Cup of Joe Unveils “Multo” Music Video Starring Miles Ocampo & Elijah Canlas
============================================================================

*   ![Image 9: Writer: Jas Rico](https://www.thenewhueph.com/post/cup-of-joe-unveils-multo-music-video-starring-miles-ocampo-elijah-canlas)
    
    [Jas Rico](https://www.thenewhueph.com/profile/thenewhue-jas/profile)
*   Apr 16
*   2 min read

Cup of Joe, the acclaimed Filipino pop band, has unveiled the [Official Music Video for their latest single "Multo"](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://www.google.com/url?q%3Dhttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v%253DCcS1fsuT10M%26amp;sa%3DD%26amp;source%3Deditors%26amp;ust%3D1744697154380786%26amp;usg%3DAOvVaw1V4gp939eUcVr_gtnuOOzo&sa=D&source=docs&ust=1744697154392770&usg=AOvVaw2DrVq-zgawbiwwDemNIB_x) featuring notable performances by actors Miles Ocampo and Elijah Canlas. This release marks a significant milestone in the band’s musical journey, offering fans a visual and auditory treat that delves into themes of love, loss, and longing.

  

“Multo,” a track from Cup of Joe's recently released album _Silakbo,_ explores the haunting memories of past relationships and the lingering emotions that accompany them. The music video artfully portrays this narrative, with the beautiful direction of Kris Cazin, adding Miles and Elijah’s compelling performances that encapsulate the song's emotional depth. The real-life couple’s on-screen chemistry brings the song's poignant lyrics to life, offering viewers a relatable and heartfelt experience.

  

Miles Ocampo, known for her versatile acting skills and previous roles in Philippine television dramas, brings a nuanced portrayal of a woman grappling with the ghosts of her past. Elijah Canlas, acclaimed for his award-winning performances in films and series, complements Ocampo’s role, adding layers of complexity to the storyline. Their collaboration in the "Multo" music video showcases their acting prowess and adds a cinematic quality to the band's musical narrative.

  

_Silakbo,_ the album featuring “Multo,” is Cup of Joe's latest offering, released on January 17, 2025. The album, which translates to "outburst" or "explosion of emotions," takes listeners on an emotional journey through ten meticulously crafted tracks, each reflecting different facets of human experiences and emotions. From upbeat melodies to soulful ballads, _Silakbo_ showcases the band's versatility and growth, solidifying their place in the contemporary Filipino music scene.

  

In support of the album, Cup of Joe has announced their "Silakbo" concert tour, set to kick off this 2025. The tour promises to bring the band's new music to fans across the Philippines, specifically in the cities of Davao and Cebu, offering live performances that capture the essence of their latest work. Tickets are now available, and fans are encouraged to secure their spots for an unforgettable musical experience.

  

The "Multo” music video is now streaming on various platforms, including YouTube and Apple Music. Fans can also listen to the full _Silakbo_ album on major music streaming services. With this release, Cup of Joe continues to captivate audiences with their heartfelt music and storytelling prowess, further establishing their footprint in the music industry.

  

For more information on Cup of Joe's _Silakbo_ album and upcoming concert tour dates, visit their official social media pages.

Cup of Joe has taken the crown as Billboard Philippines' No. 1 artist of 2025!

OPM band [Cup of Joe](https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/showbiznews/cup-of-joe-makes-history-with-billboard-ph-and-araneta-milestones/126823/) has once again ruled the music scene, dominating both fans' hearts and the charts this year.

[Billboard Philippines](https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/showbiznews/opm-artist-maki-on-topping-billboard-philippines-chart-im-really-really-happy-sa-achievement-na-iyon/115759/) announced that Cup of Joe has been named its No. 1 artist of 2025, saying: “The viral alt-pop band not only dominated the charts but also delivered music that resonated deeply with listeners.”

As Spotify Wrapped 2025 was recently launched, Cup of Joe was recognized as the most-streamed OPM artist on the platform, with their most-streamed song “Multo.”

Joining Cup of Joe in this year's Billboard Philippines top artists are Dionela, Arthur Ery, Shanti Dope, December Avenue, TJ Monterde, Ben&Ben, Earl Agustin, Hellmerry, and Maki.

Previously, the band topped the Billboard Philippines Hot 100 for 27 straight weeks with the same single, “Multo.”

The five-member band also made waves at this year's Filipino Music Awards, as their chart-topping hit “Multo” was hailed as Song of the Year, while their album _Silakbo_ proudly took home Album of the Year.

The group wrapped up their three-night “Stardust” concert series at the Smart Araneta Coliseum, held on October 10, 11, and 12.
